# Research R396 — current SYCL layer-major lifetime and callback audit

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo)

Scope: read-only source comparison of old commit `f263d87d44aa671d056c33e6c6b6b0635fc25b8c:sycl/src/prefill/prefill.cpp` and frozen current parent `8b48d17c99b70d32781f9f5b056602a598a37b1c:src/prefill/prefill.cpp` plus `include/strata/prefill/prefill.hpp`. Reviewed R394v2/R395v2 and current publication/runtime contracts. No source edits, build, tests, GPU/profiler work, Git mutation, or cleanup.

## Conclusion

The old performance claim is a real, narrowly scoped result: R394v2 records three paired 32K runs at 453.2935 tok/s baseline versus 640.3414, 646.4646, and 645.8480 layer-major, with matching complete first-logit heads and output IDs. The mechanism was all chunks of a layer before advancing, so each layer's 512 expert blobs were uploaded once rather than once per chunk. The measured candidate also held an FP32 GPU residual prefix and RAM tail. This establishes the old recipe, not a current-source speed prediction.

The old implementation must not be copied verbatim. Its `dpct::queue_ptr`, `wait()`, `dpct::sync_barrier`, `sycl::free`, old cache/source/KV structures, and destructor-time unconditional waits do not satisfy current queue and ownership contracts. A current implementation needs explicit checked drain of compute and copy queues, stager cancellation/join, and fail-stop if completion is unknown. Current `publication::cleanup_require` documents that a failed wait does not prove quiescence and exits before releasing referenced storage (`include/strata/prefill/publication.hpp`); current `Prefill::run` catch paths already apply checked `stream_sync` to both queues (`src/prefill/prefill.cpp:3297-3305`). A layer-major owner must preserve that rule for every early return and exception.

## Control flow and session state

Current `Prefill::run` owns the chunk loop at lines 1447 onward, and its inner layer loop processes [LB, LE) at 1724. Extracting that body into an internal `run_impl` and invoking it once per single-layer range is the right schedule transformation: each call walks all chunks, and the outer loop advances the layer only after its whole prompt pass. Current QSA/GDN ordinals are initialized by counting the relevant layer types below LB (1542-1543), so a one-layer range retains the correct global state ordinal. PLE is enabled only when the range includes layer 1 (1419), and the PLE operation itself is guarded by `l == 1` (1728-1730); layer-major must therefore keep layer 1 as the sole PLE mutator and preserve its original two-token predecessor. Save the incoming `ss.ple_prev`, give the PLE pass the original pair, and publish the final pair only on successful completion. The old wrapper explicitly saved `prev`, restored it before every layer (old source 1948+ and 2036), and restored the public state on success (2041+).

A normal current run updates `ss.ple_prev` after its chunk loop (3177-3179). A per-layer wrapper must avoid letting repeated internal invocations treat an already-advanced PLE predecessor as the request's input. Although PLE is active only at layer 1, failure/cancellation can happen between layer passes; do not claim a complete prompt checkpoint or callback for an intermediate-layer state.

Run only the final layer's residual through the user's public `on_chunk`, and invoke public `on_stage_chunk` only at a semantically complete checkpoint boundary. Current API documents `on_chunk` as final multi-stream residual valid through the next chunk (header 123-126); stage callback represents a point for taking that stage's state (128-132). Intermediate layer output is not the prompt's final residual and the session state is incomplete. Do not expose it as a complete checkpoint. The callback's false return or exception must still pass through checked drains before stack state is released.

Temporary lambdas must not remain in public callback members after their captures expire. Old RAII `Restore` saved the original callbacks and stage/input pointers, then restored all pointers on every exit (old source 1975-1993); however, its unconditional `m.cs->wait()/m.copy->wait()` is not a valid current drain. In a current wrapper, restore callbacks, layer range, handoff/input pointer, residency/cache aliases, residual pointers and timer contexts only after checked stream completion and stager completion. If checked completion cannot be established, fail-stop before restoration/destruction can release anything still read asynchronously. Capture the loop layer by value or keep the callback entirely local to the synchronous internal call.

Current `set_stage` and `next_` support asynchronous split-stage handoffs (header 141-153; run 3110-3126). The old layer-major implementation mutates the stage range internally, runs full prompts per layer, and assumes a final single-stage output callback. It must not be combined with split/next-stage handoff unless a separate schedule proves that intermediate bridge and stage checkpoint ordering is valid. Likewise, constrain admission around borrowed cache/phase ownership and source lifetime rather than silently replacing the decode cache mapping.

## Residual input and cache/source ownership

Old layer-major allocates a one-layer expert cache and host residency table, loads every expert of that layer, points the run at that cache, and carries the preceding layer's entire prompt residual in FP32. Its device prefix and host tail are selected per callback/chunk (old source 1947-1992, 2003-2057). The old wrapper's GPU-prefix and RAM-tail transfer logic is part of the algorithm, not an incidental optimization.

Current `hand_in_` is one pointer and the input branch copies a chunk at `hand_in_ + c0 * D` into `m.R` (current source around 1455-1460). One pointer cannot represent a bridge whose initial full chunks are device resident and later chunks are host resident. Therefore “call the extracted chunk loop unchanged for each one-layer range” is insufficient for the stated GPU-prefix/RAM-tail design. The extracted runner needs a residual-input abstraction that selects the device prefix or host tail for each chunk, or a different reviewed bridge layout. Preserve chunk-boundary alignment at the prefix/tail transition; validate row count and byte multiplication before allocation/copy.

For current source reads, preserve current `ExpertSource` contracts: non-transient blobs are resolved on the issuing thread; transient sources are read via `copy_blob` in stager jobs. Current chunk code builds jobs with source/transient metadata and uses a guarded stager drain/cancel/join (source 1561-1609, 2201+). Do not call source bookkeeping from arbitrary stager threads, retain blob pointers beyond the source's lifetime, or mark an expert reusable until its copy has completed. Before overwriting the one-layer cache for the next layer, drain compute readers and copy writers, then cancel/join/finish the stager. The current cache/borrow interfaces in header 86-95 describe decode-cache slots lent for prompt buffers; a temporary one-layer expert cache must have distinct ownership and must not alias those live buffers or phase-cache owners.

Old `ExpertTransferTimer`/phase timer contexts and host residency are stack objects. They are safe only if all asynchronous consumers are joined/drained before scope exit. Current Runtime exposes `finish(queue)` and `finish()` (runtime.hpp 62-64); prefer a checked current Runtime/stream operation with explicit error handling. A false sync or thrown wait means unknown completion, not permission to fall through to ordinary cleanup. The stream/copy queue and any additional kernel queues that read the cache must be covered by the drain proof.

## Stats, timers, cancellation, and errors

An internal layer pass will encounter current `++stats_.chunks` per chunk (1452), `stats_.tokens += T` per chunk (3107), and per-call `ms_total` accumulation near the return. With L layers, leaving these untouched reports L times the logical token/chunk totals; progress/diagnostic records keyed by chunk count can also be misleading. Aggregate request-level tokens once and logical chunks once, while preserving expert counts/host-copy timing for every layer. Keep elapsed request time as one outer interval; phase and transfer timers should explicitly include layer loads and residual movement once each. The old wrapper snapshots stats and normalizes tokens/chunks/ms_total after all passes (old 2060-2068), and its report used logical chunk count, not layer-pass count.

Cancellation must be checked before starting each layer and each chunk/pass as appropriate. Cancellation after a layer has partially advanced GDN/QSA/PLE state leaves an incomplete request and must return failure without callback/checkpoint. On callback false/throw, missing source blob, stager failure, or command-submission/wait error: cancel stager, drain checked compute/copy users, join the reader, then restore temporary state. If a checked wait reports failure or the Runtime's asynchronous exception state is unknown, process fail-stop; do not return a normal `false` while a worker, queue, pointer capture or cache reader might outlive the owner. Current `publication::cleanup_require` is the project precedent.

## Required adaptation checklist

- Use current `Runtime`/queue and current checked `publication::require`/cleanup semantics; no old `dpct` waits/free calls.
- Run one full prompt per layer range; compute QSA/GDN starting ordinals from global LB and preserve original PLE predecessor across the layer passes.
- Keep public `on_chunk` and checkpoint callbacks withheld until the final layer has completed each relevant chunk; restore callback members and stage/input pointers after checked drains.
- Add explicit per-chunk residual source selection for GPU prefix versus RAM tail; `hand_in_` alone cannot express both.
- Distinguish temporary one-layer cache from decode/borrowed/phase cache ownership; resolve stable blobs on the issuer, use current transient-source stager jobs, and drain before cache reuse.
- Count tokens/chunks once per request; count expert transfer work across every layer. Measure outer elapsed wall once.
- Fail-stop if queue completion cannot be proven before any stack capture, buffer, source, cache, or callback owner is released.
